25.0.s.en: 1. Three beautiful things and three hateful persons

25.0.0.en: 1 Three things are an adornment to me, and by them I stood up beautiful before the Lord and men: 2 agreement among brothers, love of neighbor, and harmony between a wife and her husband. 3 Three my soul hates, and I loathe their life: 4 a proud poor man, a lying rich man, and an old adulterer who has lost understanding.

25.0.1.en: Ben Sira's discourse on the three beautiful things and the three hateful things can be understood through the behavioral, personal interpretation, and also through the symbolic interpretation.

25.0.2.en: As for the behavioral interpretation of the proverb, we note the following:

25.0.3.en: a. What is beautiful in the eyes of Sirach is beautiful also in the eyes of the Lord and in the eyes of men. It is as though he affirms that the man of God does not rely on his own individual opinion, but first treasures and esteems the view of the Lord Himself, without isolating himself from people, because he is a living member of the holy congregation. It is good for a person to have his own thinking and his own evaluation of things, and at the same time for his vision to be led by the divine mind and the mind of the Church. His delight is in the Lord's good pleasure and in harmony with the Church of Christ.

25.0.4.en: b. The secret of beauty is agreement and unity through love. The common factor in the three things is love in the spirit of unity, or unity in the spirit of love.

25.0.5.en: c. The believer does not separate his family life from his social life and from the life of humanity as a whole. And although the holy and successful family is the secret of the sanctification and success of the community as a whole, he began with the brothers, that is, all mankind, followed by the neighbors and relatives, and finally the family. Thus, in the spirit of love the heart of the believer widens to include all the children of men if possible; and this will not be achieved without his caring for his relatives, and this in turn is not achieved without the sanctification of the family and its unity in the Lord.

25.0.6.en: v When the wise man enumerates the things that are counted blessings, he mentions among them "a wife who agrees with her husband" [1]; and in another place he mentions among the blessings that a woman dwells in harmony with her husband (see Sir 40:23).

25.0.7.en: In truth, from the beginning God showed a special concern for this unity, and counted the two as one. He said: "Male and female created he them" (Gen 1:27), and it is said: "There is neither male nor female" (Gal 3:28). There is no relationship between one person and another as strong as the relationship that exists between a man and his wife, if they are joined together in the Lord! Therefore, when the wise man wished to express the overflowing love in his grief for someone dear to him, he did not refer to a father or a mother or a son or a brother or a friend, but said: "Thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women" (2 Sam 1:26). Truly this love is more violent than any violence, for the other kinds (of love) are strong, but this affection is not only strong but also does not wither. There is a certain love settled in the depth of our nature, which binds our bodies to one another in an inexplicable way. From the very beginning the woman came out of the man, and after that every man and woman come forth from man and woman together (1 Cor 11:8).

25.0.8.en: Do you perceive the strength of the bond and the power of the sign? How God did not permit a different nature to intrude from outside. Observe how the arrangements were filled with divine providence! He allowed the man to marry his sister, no, not his sister but his daughter, not his daughter but something more than his daughter, she is his body! (Here he refers to the marriage of Adam to Eve.)

25.0.9.en: Thus God created all from one beginning, so that they might be joined to one another like stones in a building in one unity. He did not create her from outside, lest the man feel that she was a stranger to him, nor did He make marriage stop with her alone, lest she be confined to herself and suppose that she is the center of all (here he means that she cannot bear children without the man, otherwise she would have exalted herself over him, and love would not have arisen between them; rather her sense of need for him in order to bear fruit makes the children a sign of the union and love between them). Nothing so joins our lives together with one another as the love of a husband and his wife [1].

25.0.10.en: St. John Chrysostom As for the hateful things, we note the following:

25.0.11.en: a. The believer cannot hate persons; he hates only "their evil way of life."

25.0.12.en: b. Much has been said about caring for the poor with material, moral and spiritual giving, but poverty in itself is not a virtue; rather, if the poor man foolishly supposes that he is better than the rich man in the eyes of the Lord, then by his pride together with his poverty he becomes hateful! Riches also are not in themselves a hateful vice. The truthful rich man who realizes that all he has is a gift to him from God, that he may give from it to the poor, is righteous like Abraham, who was very rich (Gen 13:2), and like Job the rich, from whom praise did not depart even in his trials (Job 1:21). But the lying rich man is the one who reckons that his wealth is the fruit of his own intelligence or his family's, so he exalts himself in his personality or ascribes it to a wealthy family that left him a great inheritance. This rich man is a liar, because what is in his hands may be destroyed in a moment of time!

25.0.13.en: Likewise, it befits the old man to give the young what he has learned through the length of his life, with love, humility, wisdom and holiness. But if he forgets that he is human, and it befits him not to trust his body while being careless in his conduct, and he walks without wisdom, relying on his old age and long experience, he soon falls into what he did not fall into when he was young; by this he loses understanding. By this he presents a bad example to the young. It befitted white hair to be a model that the young might imitate.

25.0.14.en: As for the spiritual, symbolic interpretation, we note the following:

25.0.15.en: In the previous chapter Sirach mentioned that what he writes is prophecy (24:33), which he presents to his contemporary generation as well as to the generations to come. So what he presents here in the two proverbs is a prophecy about the Church of the Covenant, which bears the image of her Bridegroom, the Lord of glory Jesus, and which is ever renewed by the work of the Holy Spirit in her.

25.0.16.en: First: the Church of the New Testament, the holy bride of Christ.

25.0.17.en: In the spirit of prophecy he looks to the beautiful Church of the New Testament, marked by the three beautiful things in Christ Jesus:

25.0.18.en: a. The beauty of the Church is that she opens herself to humanity in love, to present to it the Savior, who is "fairer than the children of men" (Ps 45:2), whom the true believer acquires, so that His beauty is reflected upon him, and the earth becomes in his sight a radiant heaven without blemish, and he experiences a foretaste of heaven and fellowship with the heavenly ones.

25.0.19.en: b. This spiritual beauty will not be realized unless relatives are sanctified in a spirit of unity and harmony together in the Lord. These relatives are the members of the Church; and the existence of any division in her, especially among the leaders, whether men of the priesthood or monasticism, or servants, men and women, and also disputes at the level of families, or at the level of the one family, indeed at the level of the person himself, where the soul is not sanctified together with the body, and the mind with the emotions, and so on.

25.0.20.en: In all the beautiful things one notices the communal aspect: "brothers, neighbors, and a married couple." But the three kinds of people whom the soul of Sirach hates are on an individual, selfish, isolated level: "a poor man who is proud, a rich man who is a liar, and an old man who is an adulterer."

25.0.21.en: There are three things beautiful to see, and they are beautiful before the Lord and men:

25.0.22.en: Agreement among brothers, friendship among neighbors, and a wife and husband who agree well together [1].

25.0.23.en: There is no relationship between one man and another as intimate as that between a man and his wife, if they cleave to one another as they ought. Nothing is more precious than love through the wife and his love for her.

25.1.0.en: v This is the chief point, which surpasses all, good in the home: "a man and his wife agreeing" (see Sir 25:1). Where this exists, there is nothing that is not delightful. When the head is in harmony with the body, and there is no strife between them, how should all the other members not be at peace? [2]

25.2.0.en: v Nothing is more precious than to be loved in this way by a wife, and to love her [3].

25.3.0.en: v Indeed, from the beginning God showed a special provision for this unity, speaking to the two as to one person. He said: "Male and female created he them" (Gen 1:27). Again: "There is neither male nor female" (Gal 3:28). For there is no relationship between male and male as intimate as the relationship of a man with his wife, if the two are joined together as they ought [4].

25.3.1.en: St. John Chrysostom Three kinds of people my soul hates, and I loathe their way of life with utter loathing:

25.3.2.en: The proud beggar, the lying rich man, and the old adulterer who lacks understanding [2].

25.3.3.en: What does he mean by the proud poor man? By the poor man he does not mean only the person who suffers material poverty, but rather the word poor or needy means more the person who is in spiritual want. For sin makes a person needy, in need of God's mercies and help; it also carries the person who is not occupied with the temporal things of the world, but fixes his inward sight upon the Kingdom of God. The Lord Christ opened His Sermon on the Mount with His saying: "Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven" (Mt 5:3).

25.3.4.en: Origen presents to us, in his homilies on the Book of Judges, how sin drove the people into great distress, and when they cried out to the Lord in their poverty, He answered them.

25.3.5.en: v Now, these persons who were delivered up (to distress) because of sin and came into suffering, let us see what they did. Indeed it is written: "Then they cried unto the Lord in their trouble, and he saved them out of their distresses. He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and brake their bands in sunder" (Ps 107:13-14).

25.3.6.en: Add to this that each one of us, if he is small, even if he is very small, even if he is utterly insignificant by worldly standards, can act through the vice of pride, and not be among those who are so foolish and hateful (like him), not among those who are base and contemptible, according to what is stated in the Holy Scripture, like the proud poor man or the lying rich man.

25.4.0.en: Sometimes the disease of pride penetrates not only among the poor, but attacks even the order of the priests and Levites. Sometimes we find pride even among us, who ought to have been examples of humility, and who gather around the altar as a mirror for those who observe us, and yet the vice of arrogance sends out its foul and loathsome odor. So it happens that from the altar of the Lord, which requires the offering of incense of sweet fragrance, there comes forth the exceedingly foolish odor of pride and the rays of self-conceit. But this odor, which is utterly foolish, must be driven out, for the sake of heaven. Let it be driven out from the whole holy Church, especially from those who serve in the sanctuaries, that we may say with Paul that we are able to be a sweet savor of Christ (2 Cor 2:15), lest the wrath of the Lord be kindled (Ps 2:12) [5].

25.5.s.en: 2. The attractiveness of wisdom in old age

25.5.0.en: 5 If you have not stored up in your youth, how will you find in your old age? 6 How beautiful is judgment for gray hair, and good counsel for the old. 7 How beautiful is wisdom for the old, and opinion and counsel for men of glory. 8 Much experience is the crown of the old, and the fear of the Lord is their boast.

25.5.1.en: If the soul of Sirach hates the adulterous old man [2], it rejoices in the old man who has the virtue of discernment and of giving good counsel, who is adorned with wisdom and understanding, and crowned with experience of great benefit, the secret of whose glory is the fear of the Lord.

25.5.2.en: Wisdom in the life of the young man: a young man may be careless about cleaving to wisdom, postponing it to the time of his old age. If the young man does not store up wisdom, what will he gain in his old age [3]? He who cleaves to wisdom in his youth presents wise judgment in his old age, and many accept his counsel, which comes from his practical experience. Wisdom weaves a crown for the old man, indeed she becomes his crown [5]. By true wisdom the experienced old man is honored with the crown of the fear of the Lord [6].

25.5.3.en: If you have not stored up anything in your youth, how can you find anything in your old age? [3]

25.5.4.en: The young man who is serious in seeking true happiness cares for his study, his work and all aspects of his life, and benefits from the experience of those who went before him. And the young man does not forget that one day he will reach old age, and he will find many old people, men and women, suffering from emptiness with little physical effort, and sometimes suffering from weakness of memory. Therefore it befits him to look toward this coming stage with seriousness and to prepare himself for the blessed life, when in his youth he asks and strives to obtain wisdom from God and the experience of his brothers, so that he will have a reserve in his old age, when wisdom overflows from his holy mouth, and many desire to benefit from his experience. "The glory of young men is their strength: and the beauty of old men is the grey head" (Prov 20:29).

25.5.5.en: In the spirit of strength the young Daniel cried out when he saw innocent Susanna being led to death unjustly, and in the spirit of wisdom he "cried with a loud voice: I am clear from the blood of this woman" (Dan 13:45, addition). In such a young man the saying is fulfilled: "With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding" (Job 12:12). And also the saying: "The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness" (Prov 16:31).

25.5.6.en: Good discernment is the beauty of gray hair, and good counsel belongs to the old [4].

25.6.0.en: v Just as helmsmen (those who direct the rudder) and drivers of chariots gain experience in their work through discernment (wisdom in conduct) and continual striving, so also it befits those who truly seek the virtuous life to use discernment with vigilance, and to take care to live as is fitting and as is acceptable to God. For the person who desires this virtuous life and believes that he can attain his desire, receives through faith incorruption (the pure life) [6].

25.6.1.en: St. Anthony the Great Wisdom is like beauty for the old, and understanding and counsel for men of glory! [5].

25.6.2.en: Solomon the wise says: "For honourable age is not that which standeth in length of time, nor that is measured by number of years" (Wis 4:8). The honor of the old man is not in his white hair and the length of his years and experiences, for his experiences may be evil, to which he clings, reckoning them wisdom itself.

25.6.3.en: v The old man is he who goes first and hears about the work.

25.6.4.en: The old man is he who lives a great age in the faith.

25.7.0.en: The old man is he whose age is held in esteem, and whose long time is without wrinkle [7].

25.7.1.en: St. Ambrose The crown of the old is great experience, and the fear of the Lord is their glory [6].

25.8.0.en: v "Much experience is the crown of old men" (see Sir 25:6), and the whiteness of the hair is their crowns that bear witness to that experience. Nevertheless some are ashamed of the advance of years and of the whiteness of their hair [8].

25.8.1.en: St. Clement of Alexandria v One day Abba Ammon went to visit (Abba Sisoes) and found him grieved over his coming from the desert, and he said to him: Father, it is not good for you to grieve, because you have drawn near to the dwelling place of the brothers, for your body has become weak and you are no longer able to perform those works that you want in the desert.

25.8.2.en: When Abba Sisoes heard this speech he looked sharply at Abba Ammon and answered him, saying: What is this that you say to me, Abba Ammon? Was not the freedom of thoughts that I had in the desert sufficient to take the place of all the works? ... Tell me, what can you do in the desert in advanced age? And even if I am unfit for the works of the body because I have become weak through my old age, I have more ability to accomplish the works of the mind than I had in my early manhood.

25.9.0.en: 9 Nine things have I counted happy in my heart, and the tenth my tongue speaks: 10 Blessed is the man who is made glad by children, and who sees in his lifetime the fall of his enemies. 11 Blessed is he who dwells with a wise woman, and who has not slipped with his tongue, and who has not served one who is unworthy of him. 12 Blessed is he who has found prudence, and who puts his speech in a hearing ear. 13 How great is he who has found wisdom; yet he is not better than he who fears the Lord. 14 The fear of the Lord is higher than everything. 15 He who possesses it, to whom shall he be likened? 16 The fear of the Lord is the beginning of loving Him, and faith the beginning of union with Him.

25.9.1.en: Nine thoughts I count happy in my heart, and I will mention the tenth:

25.9.2.en: A father who rejoices in his children, and a man who lives and sees the fall of his enemies [7].

25.9.3.en: He presents to us ten examples of blessed people. First, blessed fathers who rejoice in their children as a gift from God (Ps 128:3-5). Next, he who sees his enemies (the devil and his hosts) fallen, having no authority over him (Ps 112:8).

25.9.4.en: St. John Chrysostom warned us against caring for the upbringing of our children out of pride, that we may be fathers of successful sons, without caring for their eternal life. What gladdens the hearts of the wise is to see their sons wise in the Lord.

25.9.5.en: A husband who is blessed because he lives with a wise wife, a man who does not slip with his tongue, and a man who does not serve one who is unworthy of him! [8]

25.9.6.en: The wise wife qualifies herself and her family for the blessed life, that is, she shares with the heavenly ones their blessed life. She reflects this blessedness upon her husband, so that the two live like two angels filled with the life of blessedness and heavenly joy. The wise man says: "House and riches are the inheritance of fathers: and a prudent wife is from the Lord" (Prov 19:14).

25.9.7.en: It is stated in the discourse of St. Gregory of Nazianzus about his parents that Gregory was drawn by his wife Nonna, not only to believe in the Lord Christ, but also to become a bishop afterward. [Behold, the good shepherd is the fruit of the prayers and guidance of his wife, and from her he learned his ideal pastoral life. With power he fled from the worship of idols, and afterward the demons began to flee from him... They became equal in prudence and splendor, zealous, supporting one another, flying above all... They had two bodies, but it was as though the two bodies had been turned into one spirit, even before their dissolution... They possessed everything and lacked nothing. They rejected wealth, and so became rich in honor... I say only one word about them, that they were truly and justly appointed, each one for his own sex: he was appointed an ornament for men, and she an ornament for women, not only an ornament, but an example of the virtuous life [9].]

25.9.8.en: "Why is he blessed who does not serve one who is unworthy of him?" He does not mean by this that the blessing arises from not serving the wicked, but from the wisdom exercised by the person who does not show partiality to a wicked man, and who, instead of supporting him to abandon evil, serves him in negligence and flattery, which drives the wicked man to persist in evil.

25.9.9.en: A man is blessed because he finds discernment!

25.9.10.en: And a man is blessed because he speaks to listening ears! [9]

25.9.11.en: When St. Abba Anthony was asked about the best of the virtues, he answered, "Discernment."

25.9.12.en: As for listening ears, this requires of us that we pray for those who listen to the voice of the Lord that we proclaim.

25.9.13.en: v You must be careful concerning whom you speak to. If you notice that this person wishes to benefit, then speak. But if not, there is no need to speak. For it is written: "Blessed is he who speaks in the ears of those who listen" (see Sir 25:9).

25.10.0.en: May you never be found giving what is holy to the dogs, or casting your pearls before swine (Mt 7:6). May the Lord grant you modesty, O brother, that you do not turn aside from the way of humility [10].

25.11.0.en: Sts. Barsanuphius and John v When St. Paul appeared before King Agrippa to answer the accusations brought against him, he wished to use a clear style for his hearers, and being confident of the success of his reasoning, he began to congratulate himself with these words: "I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews: especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews" (Acts 26:2-3). He had read Joshua (Ben Sira): "Blessed is he who tells the ears of those who listen" (see Sir 25:9). And he knew that the defender has to do with one who has influence over the judge. I also think myself happy that cultured ears should listen to my defense [11].

25.12.0.en: St. Jerome v Jeremiah was preaching the word, but no one listened to his words. So he was like the physician who wastes his medicines because of the stubbornness of his patients, who do not wish to follow his treatment or take his medicines. It is as though he were a physician saying: "I have done no good, and no one has done me any good." Perhaps the reason for the contradiction in this verse goes back to the feeling of love and affection which the person to whom good has been done bears toward the person who did him this good. It follows from this that he who preaches the word also receives good from his word (that is, he gains the love of those who hear him). And as it is written: "Blessed is he who speaks to an ear that listens" (see Sir 25:9). And the greatest good that the teacher can reap from those who hear him is that they should grow and advance, so that he may have fruit among them (Rom 1:13) [12].

25.12.1.en: v Those who are great and strong in their souls Scripture mentioned with blessing. When a person is occupied with great works, and has ambitions of worth, and continually sets before his eyes clear goals so as always to live according to the right truth, and does not even wish to look at anything trivial or small, such a person has strength and greatness in the soul. But those others who were "poor," they did not listen to the word of the Lord, as the prophet says; and, to be more precise, they did not listen because they were poor.

25.13.0.en: Therefore, since this word has been spoken to us also, let us pray to God that we may receive from Him strength and greatness enabling us to listen to those holy words, knowing that those who utter words of rebuke lose nothing as much as those who hear and do not accept this rebuke, and whom Jeremiah accuses of being poor in their minds and thoughts [13].

25.13.1.en: Origen How blessed is he who finds wisdom!

25.13.2.en: But there is no one who rises above him who fears the Lord [10].

25.13.3.en: The fear of the Lord surpasses all things, and to what can it be compared? [11]

25.14.0.en: v The fear of the Lord is the bridle that stops a person's rush toward committing evil, and pulls him backward when he is enslaved to running after his loathsome desires, not only in his outward life, but especially in his hidden inner life" [14].

25.14.1.en: v The person who lives in remembrance of God at all times is filled with fear, so that even when he resists a thought of lust passing through his soul, he becomes terrified because of this thought.

25.15.0.en: But the thought flees at once before the fear of the soul, like a bird that flees from before the person who disturbs its rest. Fear and respect for men's laws keep the body from passions. And fear and a person's shame before God keep the soul from evil thoughts. For since he knows that God sees him at all times, he watches himself continually lest he sin [15].

25.16.0.en: 17 The utmost of pain is pain of the heart, and the utmost of wickedness is the wickedness of a woman. 18 Any pain, but not the pain of the heart. 19 And any wickedness, but not the wickedness of a woman. 20 And any calamity, but not the calamity from those who hate. 21 And any vengeance, but not the vengeance of enemies. 22 There is no head worse than the head of a serpent. 23 And no wrath worse than the wrath of a woman. To dwell with a lion and a dragon is better to me than to dwell with a wicked woman. 24 The wickedness of a woman changes her appearance, and turns her face black as sackcloth. 25 Her husband is grieved among his companions, and when he hears it he sighs bitterly. 26 Every evil is slight compared to the evil of a woman. Let the lot of the sinner fall upon her. 27 As a sandy ascent is to the feet of the old man, so is a woman wicked of tongue to a quiet man. 28 Let not the beauty of a woman cause you to stumble, and do not desire a woman for her loveliness. 29 Wrath, and impudence, and great disgrace 30 is the woman who rules over her husband. 31 A wicked woman is humiliation of heart, a frowning of the face, and pain of the soul. 32 She who does not make her husband happy is but slackness of the hands and loosening of the knees. 33 From the woman sin began, and because of her we all die. 34 Do not give the water an outlet, nor a wicked woman authority. 35 If she does not walk at the beck of your hand, she will shame you before your enemies. 36 Cut her off from your body, lest she harm you continually.

25.16.1.en: Ben Sira continues to denounce the wicked wife, and each time after denouncing the wicked wife he immediately praises the good wife (26:1-6; 13-18).

25.16.2.en: Any wound but the wound of the heart, and any evil but the evil of a wife! [12]

25.16.3.en: He links the wound of the heart with the evil of the wife, to bring out that the wicked woman wounds the depths of her husband's heart and his inner feelings, even if he does not show it in his features. What is said about the wicked woman applies to the wicked husband.

25.16.4.en: Any misery, but not the misery of those who hate me!

25.16.5.en: Any vengeance, but not like the vengeance of enemies! [13]

25.16.6.en: Fierce animals may attack a man, but they bear no hatred toward him. It is said of the lion that when it has preyed upon a man and is satisfied it does not harm those around it, because it attacks the man out of its hunger and not out of hatred. It is also said of some animals and snakes that they do not attack a man when he does not attack them. So what they do by instinct is better than what the rational man does when he hates his brother.

25.16.7.en: There is no head worse than the head of a serpent, and no wrath worse than the wrath of an enemy! [14]

25.16.8.en: I would rather dwell with a lion or a serpent; it is better for me than dwelling with a wicked wife [15].

25.16.9.en: According to some modern scholars, Ben Sira is a hater of women, but other scholars have refuted this opinion, because what he wrote here concerns the wicked woman, especially as he warns his young disciples against haste in choosing a wife merely for her beauty. To the extent that he warned against wicked women, he honored and praised pious, wise women [16].

25.16.10.en: It is said that the word "head" and the word "venom" are in Hebrew "rosh." It is as though Sirach presents the following marks of the wicked woman: "vengeance" [13], "venom" [14], "preying" [15], "stings" [15], wickedness [16], and violent features [16]. Through these marks we perceive the marks of the good wife as the opposite of those of the wicked one. We find in her kindness and healing tenderness, self-giving and generosity, long-suffering with meekness, and in her love and a sincere smile are manifested.

25.16.11.en: The wickedness of a wife changes her appearance, and makes her face dark like a bear [16].

25.16.12.en: The inner wickedness of the wicked wife is reflected in her outward features: "An evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth evil; for of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh" (Lk 6:4; Mt 12:35).

25.16.13.en: Her husband goes to his neighbors to eat, and against his will he sighs bitterly [17].

25.16.14.en: As the husband's heart is crushed because of his wife's wickedness, he finds no one to support him except God, so he sighs bitterly. He is often ashamed to complain of his wife to anyone, even relatives.

25.16.15.en: All wickedness is slight compared to the wickedness of a wife.

25.17.0.en: May the lot of the sinner fall upon her [18].

25.17.1.en: God sometimes allows a sinful man a wicked wife, for his discipline. Therefore it befits one who feels that his wife is wicked, before he criticizes her, to examine himself and offer repentance for his sins.

25.18.0.en: As the climbing of a sandy hill is to the feet of an old man, so is a talkative wife to a quiet husband [19].

25.18.1.en: The quiet husband finds it difficult to cope with the chatter of the wicked wife, so his state is like that of an old man climbing a sandy hill, for he stumbles in his walking, and his feet sink into the sand, and with great difficulty he is able to move.

25.19.0.en: Do not fall because of a woman's beauty, and do not desire her beauty [20].

25.19.1.en: He who has not yet chosen a wife must seek not her beauty, but her wisdom, prudence and holiness, reckoning that dwelling with a ravening lion or a poisonous serpent is better than dwelling with a wicked wife [15-16]. Beauty is a gift from God; if it is joined with beauty of spirit in humility, the husband finds his happiness in his humble wife.

25.20.0.en: Anger, impudence and great reproach is the woman who spends upon her husband [21].

25.20.1.en: Each of the husband and the wife has a responsibility and obligation in the family; therefore the husband who in slackness does not strive to manage the financial affairs of the family is exposed to his wife's contempt.

25.20.2.en: The cause of the dejected heart, the gloomy face and the wounded heart is the wicked wife.

25.21.0.en: The wife who does not make her husband happy makes the hands limp and the knees weak [22].

25.21.1.en: The wife has her effective role in her husband's life; with wisdom she can support him so that he enjoys outstanding success, and in foolishness she can shatter his energies, gifts and abilities so that he fails.

25.22.0.en: From a woman sin had its beginning, and because of her we all die [23].

25.22.1.en: The Apostle Paul says: "Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression. Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety" (1 Tim 2:14). Some see that St. Mary conferred great honor upon women, since she bore for us the Savior. And others see that women, although they have been deprived of public teaching in the Church in the presence of men, nevertheless receive their crowns through bringing up their children in faith, love and holiness with sobriety, which men cannot do. Truly they present to the Church blessed leading members!

25.22.2.en: v Elizabeth prophesied before John. And before the birth of the Lord and Savior, Mary prophesied. Sin began from the woman, then spread to the man. In the same way salvation began first from women. Thus the rest of women can cast off the weakness of their sex, and imitate as far as possible the life and conduct of those holy women whom the Gospel describes [17].

25.22.3.en: Origen v Eve, from whom sin began, was formed from the side of the man (Gen 2:21). For she came out of his side while he slept; Christ was hanging and died on the Cross when He was wounded. Sleep and death are joined to one another, and so are the two sides: the side of Adam and the side of Christ. The Lord was wounded from where sin arose. But from the side from which Eve was formed, who by committing the fault brought death upon us, from the side of Christ the Church was formed, bestowing upon us a birth [18].

25.23.0.en: St. Augustine Give the water no passage, nor a wicked wife boldness of speech [24].

25.23.1.en: The wise man says: "The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with" (Prov 17:14). Neglect of a small wound can multiply and destroy a person's whole life. And a small breach in a ditch, if neglected, can cause a flow of abundant water that cannot be confronted. So it is with the wicked wife who does not restrain her tongue: she destroys the family.

25.24.0.en: If she does not walk according to your good direction, separate her from you [25].

25.24.1.en: v The Mosaic Law did not command divorce, but commanded the one who divorces his wife to give her a bill of divorce, because in giving her a bill of divorce there is that which calms the fury of a man's anger. So the Lord, who commanded those hard of heart to give a bill of divorce, indicated that He did not wish for divorce as far as possible. Therefore when the Lord Himself was asked about this matter He answered, saying: "Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives" (Mt 19:8). For however great the hardness of heart of the one who wishes to divorce his wife, when he knows that by means of the bill of divorce she can marry another, his anger subsides and he does not divorce her. And in order that the Lord of glory might confirm this principle, which is not to divorce a wife lightly, He made the only exception the cause of adultery. For He commanded that all other troubles (other than adultery) be endured with steadfastness for the sake of conjugal love and for the sake of chastity. And the Lord of glory confirmed the same principle by calling the one who marries a divorced woman an adulterer.

25.24.2.en: The Apostle explained this matter, saying in (Rom 7:2-3) that the wife is bound as long as her husband lives, but if her husband dies she is permitted to marry. I think that by the same rule, if the man leaves his wife, then the woman is not permitted to marry as long as her husband lives, nor the man to marry as long as the woman whom he divorced is alive [19].

25.25.s.en: Set me free from the slavery of the devil, and prepare me for the heavenly wedding!

25.25.0.en: v By my own will I was drawn to sin to enjoy its temporary pleasure, so the enemy of good hunted me and enslaved me for the sake of his kingdom.

25.25.1.en: Instead of the image of God in which I was created, corruption took hold of my nature.

25.25.2.en: True love, sincere unity and holiness ceased to be of my nature.

25.25.3.en: I fell into arrogance, lying and evil desires.

25.25.4.en: Who sets me free from the slavery of Satan but You?

25.25.5.en: v In my youth, in ignorance, I did not seek heavenly wisdom.

25.25.6.en: And the old age of helplessness came upon me while I was still young.

25.25.7.en: Behold, You open to me the doors of Your love and Your wonderful storehouses.

25.25.8.en: I cleave to You, and I come to know Your mysteries. I draw wisdom, understanding, prudence and discernment.

25.25.9.en: You crown me with the crown of love, purity and the divine fear.

25.25.10.en: I no longer fear old age, but am filled with strength.

25.25.11.en: For Your dwelling in me grants me the blessed life of the Holy Spirit.

25.25.12.en: v My thoughts have become joyful in You.

25.25.13.en: In You I enjoy fatherly love, so that every person finds in my heart a special place; I am not terrified of the devil, for in You I have crushed him under my feet.

25.25.14.en: You raise up my soul as a heavenly bride who knows no wickedness, and You set a strict guard upon my tongue.

25.25.15.en: No word will come forth except through You, O Holy One!

25.25.16.en: You grant me the spirit of discernment, so that I walk with wisdom and good management.

25.25.17.en: Your fear makes of my weakness something like a seraph or a cherub.

25.25.18.en: v Who can wound my heart while You dwell in it?!

25.25.19.en: How can I covet what my brothers have, when You are my portion?

25.25.20.en: The ancient serpent cannot swallow me, for by Your grace I do not crawl on the earth, but fly as though to heaven.

25.25.21.en: Let the devil, the savage lion, roar, and let the serpent crawl, for my heart is in Your hands!

25.25.22.en: How can my face be downcast, when Your Kingdom is established within me?

25.25.23.en: You grant to my weakness joy, gladness, glory, riches, righteousness and perfection.

25.25.24.en: I am too small to thank You and praise You!
